literal: Daojiang ranged through the classics and histories; his air was blunt and upright; he had considerable literary talent and was the coming scourge of the clan—all his uncles respected and feared him.
idiomatic: Daojiang read widely in the classics and histories, carried himself with blunt integrity, wrote well, and was the family's rising terror—uncles both respected and feared him.

literal: Prince Xie of Pengcheng and Prince Cheng of Rencheng both received him with open courtesy.
idiomatic: Princes Xie of Pengcheng and Cheng of Rencheng treated him with unfeigned respect.

literal: Xie was Grand General of the Central Army and recruited him as Traveling Aide.
idiomatic: As Grand General of the Central Army, Xie took him on as Traveling Aide.

literal: He was promoted in succession to Administrator of Yan Commandery.
idiomatic: He rose step by step to Administrator of Yan.

literal: On taking office he marked the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuanzhi and built shrines for them.
idiomatic: At his post he marked the tombs of Yue Yi and Huo Yuanzhi and raised shrines.

literal: He honored scholars, urged learning, and pressed farming and sericulture; reclaimed fields doubled yearly.
idiomatic: He honored scholars, urged study, and pushed farming—reclaimed land doubled each year.

literal: He died as Secretary of the Minister of Works, posthumously Grand Minister of Ceremonies; posthumous name Xian.
idiomatic: He died as the Minister of Works' secretary, was posthumously Grand Minister of Ceremonies with the name Xian.

literal: His writings number several tens of pieces.
idiomatic: Several dozen of his compositions survive.

literal: His son Huainzu was Erudite of the Imperial University and Supernumerary Regular Attendant; he died.
idiomatic: Son Huainzu was University Erudite and supernumerary Regular Attendant, then died.

literal: Son Zhuang had a fine name early and held the post of Commissioner of Waterways; he died in office.
idiomatic: Son Zhuang won early fame, served as Commissioner of Waterways, and died in office.

literal: Huainzu's younger brother Huairen, styled Ziyou, was learned and eloquent.
idiomatic: Huainzu's brother Huairen, styled Ziyou, was learned and articulate.

literal: His nature was tranquil; he had an easy, elegant leisure.
idiomatic: Tranquil by nature, he had an air of unhurried elegance.

literal: He served as Recorder to the Grand Minister of War and was named Administrator of Hongnong but did not take the post, settling on the border of Chenliu.
idiomatic: He was Recorder to the Grand Minister of War and named to Hongnong but never went, living on the Chenliu border.

literal: His poems, fu, inscriptions, and eulogies exceed twenty thousand words; he compiled Records of Central Tables in twenty juan.
idiomatic: He wrote over twenty thousand words of verse and prose and compiled twenty juan of Records of Central Tables.

literal: Huairen had conduct and restraint and was good at friendship.
idiomatic: Huairen was disciplined in conduct and gifted at friendship.

literal: With Wang Yan of Langye and Li Shou of Longxi he was on terms of warm affection.
idiomatic: He was close to Wang Yan of Langye and Li Shou of Longxi.

literal: He often told Yan: "In olden days Taqiu spread his way wide and Xu Shao knew him yet would not look;
idiomatic: He told Yan: "Once Taqiu walked a broad path and Xu Shao knew him yet turned away;

literal: Ji Kang stood sharp and Zhong Hui met him yet broke off speech.
idiomatic: Ji Kang stood aloof and Zhong Hui met him yet would not speak.

literal: I stand between Ji and Meng and cut away the excess."
idiomatic: I keep between those extremes and trim the excess."

literal: Yan thought this right.
idiomatic: Yan agreed.

literal: His son Yanqing was devoted to learning and in Sui held the post of Censor.
idiomatic: Son Yanqing was scholarly and in Sui became Censor.

literal: He compiled Annals of Later Wei in thirty juan.
idiomatic: He wrote thirty juan of Annals of Later Wei.

literal: In the Zhenguan era he was Magistrate of Shimen and Academician of the Eastern Palace.
idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he was Magistrate of Shimen and Eastern Palace academician.

literal: Daojiang's younger brother Daoliang, styled Zhongye, lived in seclusion and did not serve.
idiomatic: Daojiang's brother Daoliang, styled Zhongye, lived in hiding and never took office.

literal: His son Sidao.
idiomatic: His son was Sidao.

literal: Sidao, styled Zixing, was clever, sharp, handsome in debate, open and unrestrained.
idiomatic: Sidao, styled Zixing, was bright, quick-tongued, and famously unbound by convention.

literal: At sixteen Liu Song of Zhongshan wrote an inscription for someone and showed it to Sidao.
idiomatic: At sixteen, Liu Song of Zhongshan showed him an inscription he had written for another.

literal: Sidao read it and much he did not understand.
idiomatic: Sidao read it and could not follow much of it.

literal: Stirred thereby he took up books and studied under Xing Zicai of Hejian.
idiomatic: Stung to shame, he threw himself into books under Xing Zicai of Hejian.

literal: Later he wrote a piece and showed Song; Song could not understand it well.
idiomatic: Later he showed Song his own writing; Song could barely follow it.

literal: He sighed and said: "Learning has its use—was it in vain!
idiomatic: Song sighed: "So study does profit a man—it was not for nothing!
(end of quotation)

literal: He then borrowed rare books from Wei Shou.
idiomatic: He borrowed rare books from Wei Shou.

literal: Within a few years his talent and learning both stood out.
idiomatic: In a few years talent and learning both shone.

literal: Yet he did not keep his conduct and liked to slight others.
idiomatic: Yet he kept loose morals and loved to mock people.

literal: In Qi Tianbao the History of Wei was completed; Sidao disparaged it at many points.
idiomatic: When Qi's History of Wei was finished in Tianbao, Sidao tore it apart in many places.

literal: For this he was flogged again and again and sank into neglect and disorder.
idiomatic: He was beaten repeatedly for it and fell into shabby neglect.

literal: Later Left Vice Minister Yang Zunyan recommended him to court; he left the cloth for Attendant of the Minister of Works, long-term concurrent Supernumerary Regular Attendant, and duty in the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Later Yang Zunyan recommended him; he entered service as the Minister of Works' attendant, supernumerary Regular Attendant, and Secretariat duty.

literal: When Emperor Wenxuan died each leading writer composed ten dirges; the best were chosen for use.
idiomatic: At Wenxuan's death every leading writer submitted ten dirges; the best were kept.

literal: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Zu Xiaozheng, and the like had no more than one or two chosen; Sidao alone had eight.
idiomatic: Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and Zu Xiaozheng won one or two at most; Sidao alone had eight.

literal: Hence men of the time called him "Eight-Rice Lu Lang."
idiomatic: Hence his nickname: "Eight-Rice Lu Lang."

literal: Later he leaked palace talk and was sent out as Libationer of the Chancellor's Western Pavilion.
idiomatic: He leaked inner-court talk and was exiled as Libationer of the Chancellor's Western Pavilion.

literal: He served as Household Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Recorder under the Minister of Works.
idiomatic: He was heir's household attendant and recorder under the Minister of Works.

literal: In every post he was often rebuked and shamed.
idiomatic: Every office brought rebuke.

literal: Later for unauthorized use of treasury funds he was dismissed and sent home.
idiomatic: Later he was dismissed for dipping into treasury funds.

literal: Once north of Ji he gave voice to melancholy in pentasyllabic verse; the age thought it skilled.
idiomatic: North of Ji he wrote pentasyllabic verse of regret that the age praised.

literal: Later he was Supervising Secretary and Attendant at the Forest of Literature.
idiomatic: Later he was Supervising Secretary and attendant at the Forest of Literature.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi he was made Colonel Third Class and summoned to Chang'an.
idiomatic: When Zhou's Emperor Wu conquered Qi he was made Colonel Third Class and hurried to Chang'an.

literal: With peers Yang Xiuzhi and others he composed "On Hearing the Cicada."
idiomatic: With Yang Xiuzhi and others he wrote "On Hearing the Cicada."

literal: Sidao's piece, its wording clear and keen, was valued by the age.
idiomatic: Sidao's lines were clear and piercing and won the age's regard.

literal: Yu Xin of Xinye read all the co-authors and deeply admired his.
idiomatic: Yu Xin of Xinye read every contributor and marveled at his.

literal: Before long his mother fell ill and he returned home.
idiomatic: Soon his mother fell ill and he went home.

literal: He met Zu Yingbo of his commandery and cousin Changqi and others raising troops in revolt; Sidao took part.
idiomatic: He fell in with Zu Yingbo and cousin Changqi raising troops; Sidao joined them.

literal: Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju suppressed them.
idiomatic: Pillar of State Yuwen Shenju crushed the rising.

literal: Sidao's crime merited decapitation; he was already as good as dead.
idiomatic: Sidao deserved beheading and was as good as dead.

literal: Shenju had long heard his name, brought him out, and ordered him to write a victory bulletin.
idiomatic: Shenju, knowing his name, pulled him out and ordered a victory bulletin.

literal: He took brush and finished at once, the text needing no dot.
idiomatic: He wrote at a stroke, flawless.

literal: Shenju praised him and pardoned him.
idiomatic: Shenju admired him and spared his life.

literal: Later he was made Director of Instruction, Senior Grade.
idiomatic: Later he was Director of Instruction, senior grade.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was Chancellor he was moved to Administrator of Wuyang.
idiomatic: When Sui's Wendi was Chancellor he was sent to Wuyang.

literal: Rank was low and his will frustrated; he wrote "Rhapsody on the Lone Goose" to lodge his feeling.
idiomatic: Low in rank and thwarted, he wrote "Rhapsody on the Lone Goose" for his mood.

literal: Its preface reads:
idiomatic: The preface runs:

literal: In the year I set my heart on learning I left my district for the capital and at once found knowing friends; I received the favor of many lords in turn.
idiomatic: In the year I vowed myself to learning I left home for the capital, found patrons at once, and passed from one great man's favor to another.

literal: At weak-capping I had just entered the court ranks;
idiomatic: At twenty I had barely joined the court rolls;

literal: talkers erred and I stole a hollow name.
idiomatic: gossips erred, and I stole a hollow name.

literal: Men of insight from Vice Minister Yang down to Special Advance Xing and below all paid court across the threshold, met me shoe in hand, trimmed and puffed me, and raised my price.
idiomatic: From Vice Minister Yang and Special Advance Xing downward, men of insight met me at the gate, shoes in hand, polished my name, and inflated my price.

literal: Yet my talent was by nature clumsy and my disposition truly lax; profit, power, and trade I coldly would not pursue.
idiomatic: Yet talent in me was dull and nature lazy—I would not chase profit or power.

literal: Though bound in the market of court for nearly thirty years, the heart that walks alone never left my breast.
idiomatic: Though the court held me thirty years, the lone heart never left my breast.

literal: My regimen was out of harmony and I had a slight breath ailment.
idiomatic: Care of life went awry and I had a slight breath sickness.

literal: With a tally I sat and whistled, guarding the eastern plain.
idiomatic: With seal in hand I governed the eastern plain.

literal: On the mighty river's bank the fertile fields stretched wide; clamor was shut out and fish and birds were neighbors.
idiomatic: Along the great river fertile fields ran to the horizon; noise fell away and fish and birds were my neighbors.

literal: A goose apart from the flock was taken by a fowler; a rustic tamed it and presented it to me.
idiomatic: A stray goose was netted; a countryman tamed it and gave it to me.

literal: I set it in the pool garden and admired it morning and evening; it eased sorrow and lightened illness.
idiomatic: I kept it in the pool court, admired it dawn and dusk; it eased grief and lightened sickness.

literal: The Changes says "the goose advances on the land"—its feathered majesty.
idiomatic: The Changes says the goose "advances on the land"—ceremonial splendor.

literal: Yang Xiong says "the goose flies in the dark"—soaring height.
idiomatic: Yang Xiong says "the goose flies in the dark"—lofty flight.

literal: Huainanzi says "eastward to Jieshi"—fleeing summer heat.
idiomatic: Huainanzi says "east to Jieshi"—escaping summer's steam.

literal: Zhang Heng's fu says "southward to Hengyang"—shunning severe cold.
idiomatic: Zhang Heng's rhapsody says "south to Hengyang"—fleeing bitter cold.

literal: In elegant step and clear tone, far heart and high rhyme, even the yuan and luan descend—rare is his peer.
idiomatic: In grace of gait and clarity of song, heart distant and tone high—even phoenix birds stoop; few match him.

literal: Yet with wings clipped in the wall's shade he stands alone in paired shadow, pecking chaff, keeping company with chickens— is it not pitiable?
idiomatic: Yet wings clipped in the courtyard shade he stands alone, pecking chaff beside barnyard fowl—is it not pitiable?

literal: My fifty years have suddenly arrived; speaking forever of life's affairs, I am moved to many threads, and so I write this fu to console myself.
idiomatic: Fifty years come sudden; brooding on life's business stirs many threads—thus this fu, to comfort myself.

literal: At the start of Kaihuang, because his mother was old, he memorialized asking to leave office; a gracious edict permitted it.
idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, his mother being old, he asked to resign; a kind edict allowed it.

literal: Sidao relied on talent and standing and often bullied others; hence his official path sank and stalled.
idiomatic: Sidao leaned on talent and rank, bullied many, and his career stalled.

literal: Then he also wrote "On Toiling Life," cutting at the present age.
idiomatic: He then wrote "On Toiling Life," skewering his own times.

literal: After more than a year he was ordered by edict to greet the Chen envoy in the suburbs.
idiomatic: A year on, edict ordered him to greet Chen's envoy in the suburbs.

literal: Soon he was in mourning for his mother.
idiomatic: Soon he mourned his mother.

literal: Before long he was recalled as Regular Attendant and assisted the Vice Director of the Secretariat.
idiomatic: Soon he was Regular Attendant assisting the Secretariat vice director.

literal: At that time they debated establishing the Six Ministers and were about to appoint the Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: Court debated the Six Ministers and meant to seat the Minister of Justice.

literal: Sidao memorialized: "The Department has a Bureau of Transport; the Temple keeps the Minister of the Imperial Stud;
idiomatic: Sidao wrote: "The ministry keeps Transport while the temple keeps the Stud—

literal: the Department has a Bureau of Punishments; the Temple removes the Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: the ministry keeps Punishments while the temple drops Justice.

literal: That values livestock and cheapens punishment— truly it cannot be."
idiomatic: That exalts herds and cheapens law—unacceptable."

literal: He also stated that the palace hall is no place for flogging; when courtiers merit the bastinado, ransom should be allowed.
idiomatic: He also said the throne hall is no beating ground—when courtiers deserve the rod, let them redeem the blow.

literal: The emperor praised and adopted it all.
idiomatic: The emperor praised and took all of it.

literal: That year he died in the capital.
idiomatic: That year he died in the capital.

literal: The emperor greatly regretted it and sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice.
idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and sent envoys to sacrifice.

literal: Twenty juan of his collected works circulate in the world.
idiomatic: Twenty juan of his works circulate.

literal: His son Chisong in the Daye era was Magistrate of Hedong.
idiomatic: Son Chisong in Daye was Magistrate of Hedong.

literal: Daoliang's younger brother Daoyu, styled Ningzu.
idiomatic: Daoliang's brother Daoyu, styled Ningzu.

literal: Young he was famed for devotion to learning; his bearing was also beautiful.
idiomatic: Young he was famed for scholarship and handsome bearing.

literal: He married the Princess of Lelang, daughter of Emperor Xianwen, and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: He married Emperor Xianwen's daughter, Princess of Lelang, and became Commandant of the Horse Guards.

literal: Daoqian loved the study of the Rites and disputed more than seventy articles in Minister Wang Jian's "Collected Notes on Mourning Garments."
idiomatic: Daoqian loved ritual studies and challenged more than seventy articles in Wang Jian's "Collected Notes on Mourning Garments."
